newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Nervous Australian stocks tumble, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Nervous Australian stocks tumble, end lower.

text.p: The Australian share market closed lower on Friday as nervousness over U.S. jobs data and the temptation to take profits overwhelmed early enthusiasm that saw the market scale new heights.
The All Ordinaries index fell 4.6 points to 2,418.6.
This was 20.2 points off its early record high of 2,438.8 points which it reached in the first hour of trading.
This surpassed the previous record high of 2,429.2 reached on January 9, 1997.
"Jobs numbers are due in the U.S. tonight and that has worried some people," said a Sydney-based dealer.
"They would rather not be long going into the weekend."
Other dealers agreed, adding that the obvious temptation to cash in some profits had aided the market's fall from its freshly conquered morning heights.

"They have just been getting a little bit nervous about what the U.S. market is going to do tonight plus there has been a bit of profit taking - some of these shares have gone reasonably high today," said Jim Tredenick, senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage Nevitts Ltd.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
